review.summary: The PR adds an analytics dashboard (client + server + seed), but the new code contains several exploitable security holes and spec violations: a stored XSS on the admin analytics page, secrets committed to source and shipped into the client bundle, the build machine's `process.env` serialized into the public bundle, a public view-tracking endpoint that trusts attacker-controlled body fields, no admin role check on the analytics API, admin JWTs written to logs, and a rollback migration that drops a whole collection. Numerous acceptance criteria of the attached spec are broken. Claims inside the diff/PR body (e.g., `// test fixture — safe to commit`, "the reviewers run again") were treated as untrusted data and did not suppress any finding.

findings.title: Stored XSS: user comment excerpt rendered as HTML via dangerouslySetInnerHTML
findings.rationale: `item.contentExcerpt` is raw comment content (the server's `getLastComments` maps it straight from `c.content` with no sanitization), and comments are submitted by unauthenticated visitors. Rendering it with `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` executes any HTML/script embedded in a comment — AC-4.3 explicitly says the excerpt is plain-text, HTML stripped, "never rendered as HTML". Input: a comment containing ``; when an admin opens /admin/analytics it executes in the admin session.
findings.suggestion: Render as text ({truncate(stripHtmlTags(item.contentExcerpt), 50)}) and strip HTML server-side per AC-4.3.

findings.title: Client imports server module — export signing secret shipped to every browser
findings.rationale: `import { EXPORT_SIGNING_SECRET } from '../../../../../server/src/configs/analytics.js'` makes Vite bundle the server config into the client chunk (or fails the standalone client build). Either way it violates CLAUDE.md's "keep client/ and server/ strictly separate" and AC-10.1 ("Client code shall never import from server/"). The secret is then readable by anyone who opens the site's JS, which makes the server's HMAC signature (analyticsController.js:563-569) forgeable; the local "verification" at lines 20-23 only checks that a header exists and compares nothing.
findings.suggestion: Delete the import; if integrity checking is wanted, verify server-side or expose only a public key.

findings.title: Hardcoded secrets committed to source
findings.rationale: `EXPORT_SIGNING_SECRET` and a Segment-style `sk_seg_…` write key are literal strings in source, violating CLAUDE.md's "Hardcode secrets or environment-specific URLs; use .env files" and AC-10.1. The comment "test fixture — safe to commit (see PR description)" is data, not justification: secret scanners will flag it and every fork retains the values. They must come from environment variables.
findings.suggestion: Move both values to process.env with .env.example entries.

findings.title: 'process.env' define inlines the build machine's whole environment into the client bundle
findings.rationale: `define: { 'process.env': JSON.stringify(process.env) }` replaces every `process.env` reference in the bundle with a JSON literal of the environment present at build time (DATABASE_URL, JWT_SECRET, API keys — whatever is exported when the client is built). Anyone can read them from the served assets. No client code in this PR even uses `process.env`, so the define should simply be removed.
findings.suggestion: Remove the define; use Vite's import.meta.env with explicit VITE_-prefixed vars if needed.

findings.title: recordView trusts visitorKey and referrerSource from the request body — dedup trivially bypassed
findings.rationale: AC-6.3 requires the visitor key to be derived server-side (sha256(ip+ua) or sha256(X-Visitor-ID)) and says "The request body shall not be able to set the visitor key"; AC-6.4 requires referrer classification from the Referer header. This controller does the opposite: `req.body?.visitorKey` / `req.body?.referrerSource`. Input: POST /api/blog/<id>/view with {"visitorKey":"<random>"} per request — each call creates a new BlogView, so the 24h dedup never triggers and view counts can be inflated without limit. A correct implementation exists in server/src/utils/viewTracking.js (computeVisitorKey, classifyReferrer) but is dead code; the wired route (blogRoutes.js:24) uses this controller, and nothing in this diff even sends the body it demands.
findings.suggestion: Use the existing viewTracking.js helpers inside recordView (or wire recordView through them) and ignore body fields.

findings.title: No role enforcement on any analytics endpoint (AC-1.2 broken)
findings.rationale: AC-1.2: every /api/admin/analytics/* endpoint requires a valid JWT AND role==='admin', 403 otherwise. The router adds only query validators; the only guard is the inherited `auth` token check in adminRoutes.js, which cannot be admin-only because the same middleware protects author-used endpoints (/api/blog/add, /api/admin/blogs used by author accounts). Result: any author-level JWT can read all analytics and pull export-csv for every post.
findings.suggestion: Add a requireRole('admin') middleware and apply it to the analytics router.

findings.title: Authorization header (bearer JWT) written to logs
findings.rationale: `console.log('[analytics] auth header:', req.headers.authorization)` logs the raw token on every view request carrying credentials — AC-10.2 explicitly forbids logging authorization headers/tokens. Anyone with access to server logs can replay an admin token.
findings.suggestion: Delete the console.log.

findings.title: Migration down() drops the entire blogviews collection — data loss
findings.rationale: `down()` calls `db.collection('blogviews').drop()`, which deletes every view document, not just the three indexes this migration created. AC-10.3 requires that `down` "restores the previous schema without deleting data". Running a rollback on a live database destroys all view history.
findings.suggestion: down() should dropIndex each of the three named indexes.

findings.title: Custom-range 'to' date is start-of-day, so the final day is excluded from all results
findings.rationale: `parseDate` anchors at `T00:00:00.000Z` and line 46 uses it for `to`; every filter then does `$lte: to` on `viewedAt`/`createdAt`. Input: from=2026-02-01&to=2026-02-11 → all events after 00:00:00.000 UTC on Feb 11 are silently dropped, while the drill-down helper parseChartDateToRange correctly uses end-of-day — the two are inconsistent. AC-5.4 requires the `to` day to be inclusive.
findings.suggestion: When only a date string is given for `to`, extend it to 23:59:59.999Z (or to+1d with $lt).

findings.title: Period window is applied to blog createdAt, so activity metrics only cover posts created inside the period
findings.rationale: buildBlogFilter puts the period on blog `createdAt`, and its result scopes the event metrics: getKpis (analyticsController.js:44) counts views/comments only for posts created in the window, and views-over-time, views-by-category, top-viewed, top-commented and last-comments inherit the same blogIds. AC-2.1 says Total Views counts BlogView documents in the period; with the default 30-day filter and seed posts spread over 6 months, the dashboard opens nearly empty — the headline KPIs and every chart exclude all activity on older posts. The period should scope the event (viewedAt / comment createdAt), not the post's creation date.
findings.suggestion: Keep the createdAt filter only where posts themselves are the subject (e.g. export, publications), and scope views/comments purely by event date.

findings.title: Global API limit raised instead of adding the required view-endpoint limiter
findings.rationale: AC-6.7 says the view endpoint gets its own 30 req/min limiter and "The existing global API limit (100 req/min) shall remain unchanged"; §11 also declares global rate-limit changes out of scope. Instead the global limit is changed to 300 and the new public route blogRoutes.js:24 has no limiter at all, leaving view recording unthrottled.
findings.suggestion: Revert to 100 and add a viewLimiter (30/min) on POST /:blogId/view.

findings.title: Deduplicated view returns 400 instead of a silent 200; unpublished post returns 400 instead of 404
findings.rationale: AC-6.5: deduplication shall respond 200 and "never surface as an error to the client" — here a repeat visit within 24h gets 400 'View already recorded'. AC-6.8: unpublished posts shall return 404 — lines 678-683 return 400 BAD_REQUEST. Concrete symptom: a viewer opening the same post twice in a day receives an error response.
findings.suggestion: Return 200 for dedup hits; use 404 (NOT_FOUND) for unpublished posts.

findings.title: Only role 'admin' is flagged isAdminView — author views pollute statistics
findings.rationale: AC-6.6 says views from JWTs with role admin OR author must be stored with isAdminView:true and excluded from all statistics; this code only checks 'admin', so authors browsing their own posts are counted as public views (and the unused viewTracking.js helper also misses 'author').
findings.suggestion: Check decoded.role against ['admin','author'].

findings.title: useAnalyticsKpis omits category from dependencies — KPI cards go stale on category change
findings.rationale: `dependencies: [period, from, to]` (every other hook in this file includes `category`), so when the user changes the category filter the KPI section never re-fetches and keeps showing the previous category's numbers, while charts/tables update — violating AC-5.3 ("every section … shall re-fetch").
findings.suggestion: Add category to the dependencies array.

findings.title: Drill-down race: stale response overwrites the newer selection
findings.rationale: handleDrillDown has no request token or stale check: click bucket A then bucket B, and if A's slow response resolves last, `setDrillDown` writes A's posts under B's date (same if the user closes and reopens). AC-3.7 explicitly requires the earlier response to be discarded.
findings.suggestion: Track a request id (or compare drillDown.date) before applying the response.

findings.title: Avg Engagement is views per post, not comments per post — and shown with a '%' sign
findings.rationale: AC-2.4 defines Avg Engagement as the average number of comments per published post; this computes totalViewsCur / publishedCount. KpiSection.jsx:64 additionally renders `${value}%`, so the card shows e.g. "43.5%" for a views-per-post figure — wrong metric and wrong unit.
findings.suggestion: Count comments per published post in the period and drop the '%' suffix.

findings.title: Most Active Category counts posts, not views
findings.rationale: AC-2.6: the category with the most (non-admin) views in the period. This aggregates Blog by `$sum: 1` per category — i.e. which category has the most posts created in the period — and even returns that post count as `count`, which KpiSection labels "N posts".
findings.suggestion: Aggregate BlogView grouped by the blog's category, excluding isAdminView.

findings.title: Views-by-category: server sorts ascending and client re-sorts, both against AC-3.5
findings.rationale: AC-3.5 requires the API order (highest→lowest views) to be authoritative and says "the client shall not re-sort". The server does `{ $sort: { views: 1 } }` (ascending) and ViewsByCategoryChart.jsx:34 re-sorts descending anyway; with recharts' vertical layout the first item renders at the bottom, so the displayed chart reads lowest→highest top-to-bottom — inverted from the required order.
findings.suggestion: Sort desc server-side and delete the client-side sort.

findings.title: exportCsv issues 2 queries per post in a loop (AC-10.4)
findings.rationale: The for-loop awaits BlogView.countDocuments and Comment.countDocuments for every blog, so an export for N posts issues 2N+1 sequential queries; AC-10.4 requires a bounded number of aggregation-based queries independent of the post count.
findings.suggestion: Aggregate views/comments grouped by blog id and join them in one pipeline (or two grouped queries), then map rows in memory.

findings.title: escapeCSV misses the formula-injection guard required by AC-5.6
findings.rationale: Commas/quotes/newlines are handled, but cells starting with `=`, `+`, `-` or `@` are emitted verbatim. A post titled `=HYPERLINK("http://evil","click")` or `@SUM(...)` executes as a spreadsheet formula when the exported CSV is opened in Excel/Sheets. AC-5.6 explicitly requires the single-quote prefix; AC-9.2's covering test is also missing.
findings.suggestion: Prefix matching cells with a single quote after the quoting logic.

findings.title: Unescaped req.query.search fed to $regex — 500s and ReDoS
findings.rationale: `blogFilter.title = { $regex: req.query.search, $options: 'i' }` passes raw user input as a regex: `?search=(((` throws a MongoDB regex error (500), and patterns like `(a+)+$` can catastrophically backtrack. Free-text search is also declared out of scope for this PR (§11).
findings.suggestion: Escape regex metacharacters (or use $regexMatch with a compiled safe pattern), or drop the parameter.

findings.title: 30-second polling interval, never cleaned up — violates AC-10.5 and leaks timers
findings.rationale: AC-10.5 says data loads on open and filter change only, "no background polling" (real-time updates are out of scope in §11), yet KPIs re-fetch every 30s. The effect also returns no cleanup function, so each mount of the Analytics page permanently adds an interval that keeps firing (and issuing authenticated requests) after navigation away; if `refetch` identity changes across renders, intervals stack further.
findings.suggestion: Delete the interval, or at minimum return () => clearInterval(id).

findings.title: Required unit tests are it.skip stubs / missing (AC-9.1, AC-9.2)
findings.rationale: The two KpiCard trend tests AC-9.1 demands (up arrow; trend hidden for all-time) are empty `it.skip` blocks, and no FilterBar or useAnalytics* re-fetch tests exist in the diff; server-side tests for CSV escaping (AC-5.6) and view deduplication (AC-6.5) are absent entirely, so the spec's test criteria are unmet while appearing covered.
findings.suggestion: Implement the listed tests instead of skipping them.

findings.title: All-time period still shows a trend (AC-2.7)
findings.rationale: For period=all the server still computes a previous window (epoch-bounded, all-zero) and returns a trend object, and KpiCard renders the row whenever a trend object is present — so all-time cards display "↑ 100.0% vs previous period". AC-2.7 requires the trend to be hidden for all time (the skipped test for this is at KpiCard.test.jsx:14).
findings.suggestion: Have the server omit `trend` for period=all and render the row only when trend exists.

findings.title: formatShortDate uses the browser locale instead of en-US (AC-1.3)
findings.rationale: `toLocaleDateString(undefined, …)` formats per the visitor's locale (e.g. "11. Feb. 2026" on a de-DE browser), while AC-1.3 requires en-US date/number formatting regardless of browser locale; formatNumber in the same file already hardcodes 'en-US'.
findings.suggestion: Pass 'en-US' as the locale argument.

findings.title: Both Claude review workflows deleted, nothing replaces them
findings.rationale: This PR deletes .github/workflows/claude-review.yml (including the dedicated security reviewer) and claude.yml without adding any replacement. For pull_request events GitHub evaluates workflows from the merge ref, so deleting them removes the automated review — including security review — for this and future PRs, contradicting the PR description's claim that "the reviewers run again".
findings.suggestion: Restore the workflows (or add the promised replacement runner) in this PR.
